A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VidCom2 research. All pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, inference-efficiency measurements, ablations and appendix sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds EgoSchema and PerceptionTest comparisons and a window-size ablation.

M1.justification: The two-stage compression method, Equations 3–10 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Local-window variants appear in a new ablation; global pooling remains the default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated EgoSchema and PerceptionTest coverage while retaining the original four benchmarks. Table 3 and Appendix A extend evaluation with focused first-person procedural and temporal reasoning, and perceptual video question answering, substantially broadening the represented evaluation data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. New Table 3 uses already evaluated FastV, PDrop and DyCoke; newly cited compression papers are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds a controlled comparison of representation windows spanning 4, 8, 16 and 32 frames, holding input length at 32 frames on LLaVA-OV-7B. This introduces an additional experimental protocol without revising the retained experiments.

E4.justification: New Table 7 tests whether local or global context better supports frame-compression adjustment. This is one additional design ablation; the previous component ablations, Appendix D sensitivity study and Appendix F visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables and plots retain their results. New Table 3 reports VidCom2 scores of 59.7 and 56.7 on EgoSchema and PerceptionTest, versus DyCoke's 59.5 and 56.4 at 25% retention. Table 7 adds window-size results, forming a bounded extension of the findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–10 and algorithmic formulas are unchanged. The new window-size discussion supplies empirical evidence and interpretation, without adding formal derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same frame-uniqueness, compatibility and efficiency claims, including 99.6% performance retention and 70.8% lower LLM generation latency. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation that larger representation windows improve performance, with small differences between 16 and 32 frames, and favors global context for long videos. The limitations concerning larger models and streaming applications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new window study's sizes and fixed 32-frame setup, and acknowledges Ascend 910 processor support. The code link, algorithm details, temperature, epsilon and stated A100 experimental platform remain unchanged; the acknowledgment does not establish a hardware switch.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to newer compression research, including Chen et al. (2025) and Ma et al. (2025), and the two additional benchmarks. The research positioning remains stable. The retitled Liu et al. reference retains arXiv 2501.05179 and represents an existing work.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewriting in Section 4.2, an additional analysis passage, expanded benchmark descriptions and acknowledgments. The overall section structure is preserved. Appendix A introduces a duplicated introductory sentence.

P2.justification: v2 adds compact Tables 3 and 7 and relocates existing ablation tables and Figure 5 through page reflow. Existing diagrams, plots and appendix visualizations retain their content and design; the two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmark comparisons and local-versus-global ablation strengthen empirical support beyond v1, without changing the method or original findings. These limited gains are tempered by an unexplained reporting discrepancy: identical component scores receive averages of 100.1 in new Table 7 and 100.3 in retained Table 8.
